name: value_weighted_order_preemption
patch_description:
Implement Value-Weighted Order Preemption for the 10-order market order limit.

Previously, `_add_sell` checked `if len(orders) < 10:` and silently dropped any new sell order when 10 orders were present. Furthermore, all selling loops (shed pressure valve, oracle front-running, town-shop harvesting, high-value asset pre-liquidation, and phased day-29 liquidation) contained short-circuit checks (`len(mkt) < 10` or `if len(mkt) >= 10: break`). Consequently, when the 10-order cap was reached—often filled by low-margin baseline orders or minor batches of low-price goods such as WHEAT ($25) or CARROT ($35)—vital high-revenue orders (such as MELON at $250, WOOL at $200, or large front-run batches) were silently dropped or never evaluated.

This edit:
1. Enhances `_add_sell` with value-weighted preemption:
   - Consolidates into an existing sell order for the product (without consuming a new order slot).
   - If under the 10-order limit, appends normally.
   - If at the 10-order limit, evaluates the total expected revenue (`qty * price`) of the candidate order versus all existing `SELL` orders. If the candidate order is worth more than 1.1x the lowest-value existing sell order, the low-value order is preempted and replaced.
2. Removes the restrictive `len(mkt) >= 10: break` guards in the selling loops so high-value items can always be evaluated and consolidate or preempt low-value orders.
3. Consolidates redundant order-checking logic into the `_already_selling` helper and enables phased day-29 liquidation starting at step 693 with batch 7 for superior late-game volume throughput.
